payload.feature:
Judge and ship Phase 2 slice (i): a world of two DISTINCT repositories, already implemented on this branch.

The implementation is COMMITTED on this branch, in two commits off origin/main:
  8c80277 realms: a world of two repositories resolves each realm to its own tree
  68116ee realms: four surfaces answer for a second repository

There is nothing left to implement. If the implement seat agrees the work is complete, it says so and hands on without rewriting it; it changes code ONLY to fix a defect it finds, or to close a finding the reviewers raise.

What the branch claims, and what the gates must judge:
Every multi-realm map exercised before this branch pointed its realms at ONE tree — brokkr-runtime built alpha, beta, gamma and delta all at path 'brokkr'; brokkr-cli built alpha/beta and alpha/ghost both at '.'; brokkr-core's a/b/c are shape-only because that crate does no I/O (decision 0003). No test had ever handed the machine two real repositories at two different HEADs. The branch builds that fixture and proves five things through surfaces that already exist: path resolution and realm_for per tree; 'brokkr realms' printing each realm's own head; 'brokkr doctor' naming the failing REALM rather than a broken world; realm_facts keyed per realm with its own head, drift and dirty worktree; and the fleet readouts across two hearths, read side by side and never merged (decision 0026 rulings 3 and 5).

Judge it as evidence, not as a feature. It is deliberately the smallest possible slice — the ground decision 0023 ruling 7 (Bifroest crossings, still unruled) stands on. Tests and fixtures only: no new schema version, no new contract, no engine behaviour change, no new CLI flag. A change that adds any of those is out of scope for this slice and should be a finding, not a commit.

Verify seat: run the gates the contribution policy requires and report exactly what passed. Reviewers: check that the fixture is honest — two repositories with genuinely different HEADs, assertions that would FAIL if both realms resolved to one tree, and no test that merely restates an existing one-tree test under a new name.

instructions.analyze:
# OpenSpec analyze

Judge duplication, ambiguity, underspecification, house alignment, coverage gaps, and inconsistency across proposal, deltas, design and tasks. Treat the realm house as the constitution. Return each finding with severity and its earliest owning artifact; zero findings is consistent.
instructions.clarify:
# OpenSpec clarify

Judge underspecified areas, unquantified language, missing decisions, capability/delta mismatches, and requirements without adequate scenarios. Return every ambiguity with the evidence needed to settle it; zero findings is clear.
instructions.design:
# OpenSpec design

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/design.md`. Record context, goals and non-goals, decisions with alternatives, risks, migration, and open questions. On return, revise the design and dependent artifacts so no finding is merely acknowledged.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.

# OpenSpec tasks

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/tasks.md` as numbered groups of checkboxes. Name the requirement served by every task. On return, repair the breakdown and its requirement coverage before implementation resumes.

# OpenSpec return

Change location: `openspec/changes/{change}`. Archive operation: ["openspec","archive","{change}","--yes"].

# OpenSpec archive

Folding a change is the last task: run the archive operation named above,
which moves the change directory under `openspec/changes/archive/` and
folds its deltas into `openspec/specs/`. Folding also records which change
wrote which capability, so every capability the change touched carries a
`## Provenance` list.

After the archive operation, open each capability's
`openspec/specs/<capability>/spec.md` that the change touched and append
exactly one line under a `## Provenance` heading held at the end of the
file:

`- \`<archived-directory-name>\` — folded <YYYY-MM-DD>`

`<archived-directory-name>` is the directory the archive operation
created under `openspec/changes/archive/`; `<YYYY-MM-DD>` is the day it
was folded. Append only: never rewrite, reorder or remove an existing
provenance line, because standing truth accumulates and is not edited into
a different meaning. The line is a pointer, not a summary — it names the
change and nothing else, and the why stays in the change directory.

house.content:
This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, `policy/schemas/`, and `reference/` are read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `bundles/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

## Release configuration

The release manager prepares the candidate and profile patches; the operator
publishes them. Local validation is preparation work. Remote CI on the final PR
head, publication, channel updates and live-profile verification are handoff
steps, recorded as pending until their remote results exist. Historical
"live from" channel versions and old journal examples are historical facts,
not current-version references to replace.

```json
{
  "repository": "feedback-loop-ai/brokkr",
  "default_branch": "main",
  "tag_format": "v{version}",
  "version_files": ["Cargo.toml", "Cargo.lock"],
  "version_update": "Bump the workspace package and six path-dependency versions together. Run cargo update --workspace --offline without upgrading registry dependencies. Measure and update the witness and compose manifest digests because the engine version participates in their identity.",
  "release_notes": "docs/releases/v{version}.md",
  "handoff_directory": "docs/releases/v{version}",
  "scratch_directory": ".forge/release",
  "documentation": ["README.md", "ARCHITECTURE.md", "CONTRIBUTING.md", "docs/guides/", "packaging/README.md"],
  "validation": [
    {"name": "format", "command": "cargo fmt --all -- --check"},
    {"name": "clippy", "command": "cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings"},
    {"name": "tests", "command": "cargo test --workspace --all-features --locked"},
    {"name": "self bundle", "command": "cargo run --locked -p brokkr-cli -- compile --bundle bundles/self"},
    {"name": "verify bundle", "command": "cargo run --locked -p brokkr-cli -- compile --bundle bundles/verify"},
    {"name": "exact coverage", "instructions": "Run bash scripts/coverage-exact.sh in CI or host validation outside the workspace box before tagging. Boundary tests require creating a namespace, which the box deliberately refuses to nest. Record this check as pending in the preparation handoff until that external result exists; never lower the coverage gate."},
    {"name": "release binary", "command": "cargo build --release --locked -p brokkr-cli"},
    {"name": "remote CI", "instructions": "Before tagging, require all applicable CI jobs on the final candidate commit, including all three operating systems, MSRV, licenses, audit, packaging and exact coverage."}
  ],
  "organization_profiles": [
    {"repository": "feedback-loop-ai/.github", "path": "profile/README.md", "project_url": "https://github.com/feedback-loop-ai/brokkr", "apply": "after verified publication"}
  ],
  "channels": [
    {"name": "GitHub release", "evidence": "Five platform archives, Linux deb/rpm packages, SHA256SUMS and signed build provenance."},
    {"name": "crates.io", "evidence": "All seven workspace crates serve the new version."},
    {"name": "apt and rpm", "evidence": "The signed Pages repositories index the new packages."},
    {"name": "Homebrew, Scoop and Nix", "evidence": "The generated channel PRs are merged and their versions and digests match the release manifest."}
  ],
  "extensions": [
    {"name": "workflow toolchain agreement", "instructions": "Check that CI, release admission and local coverage select the same pinned compiler.", "evidence": "Both workflows and coverage-exact.sh consume rust-nightly-version.txt."},
    {"name": "frozen contracts", "instructions": "Compare contracts, fixtures, policy/phase-machine.json and reference against the previous release; explain additive versions and flag modifications to frozen bytes.", "evidence": "A reviewed diff with migration notes for any new contract versions."}
  ]
}
```

result.notes: Framed the judge-and-ship task: work is already committed (8c80277, 68116ee) implementing all five proofs of Phase 2 slice (i) — two real git repositories at two different HEADs exercised through World resolution, `brokkr realms`, `brokkr doctor`, engine `realm_facts`, and the fleet readouts (`runs`, `muninn`). Diff confirmed tests/fixtures only plus one #[cfg(test)] visibility widening; contracts/policy/reference/fixtures/decisions/Cargo files untouched. Task file names the goal (judge, don't reimplement), the exact tests that must stay green, two documented residuals reviewers should not ask to be 'fixed' in this slice, non-goals, the gate list verify must run, and an honesty checklist for reviewers to confirm the two-repository dimension is genuinely exercised rather than restating a one-tree test.

gates_pending: scripts/coverage-exact.sh (boundary tests need a namespace the box refuses to nest; host/CI only)
inputs.mutation_check: each proof re-run against a deliberately one-tree fixture and observed to FAIL on its own two-repository assertion
residuals_recorded: report_realm_house_for_world aggregates all realms into one world-wide ok count; a healthy realm's line vanishes when a neighbour's house is broken (asserted as today's behaviour, doc-commented as the residual)
a single run's realm_facts can carry only one realm key by construction (0026 binds a run to one realm); not a defect, doc-commented so a later crossing slice does not read it as a law

result.notes: Judged the two committed commits as evidence; found no defect and changed no code. Read every hunk of the 821-line diff: the only non-test line is `#[cfg(test)] mod tests;` -> `pub(crate) mod tests;` in crates/brokkr-runtime/src/realms.rs, a test-only visibility widening that compiles out of release builds. No new schema version (forge.realms/v2 predates the branch), no new contract, no engine behaviour change, no new CLI flag; contracts/, policy/, reference/, fixtures/, docs/decisions/, Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock are untouched. All seven new tests pass by name. Beyond running them green I tested that they are load-bearing: mutating each fixture into a one-tree world (beta's realm path repointed at alpha, and beta's staged run driven in alpha's tree) made every proof FAIL on its own two-repository assertion -- realms::tests proof 1 on path_of, engine proof 4 on realm_facts becoming unkeyed, the CLI realms verb on printing alpha's sha for beta, and the runs and muninn fleet proofs on recorded_heads reading {"alpha": ...} where {"beta": ...} was required. Mutations reverted; working tree is clean and byte-identical to 68116ee. The doctor proof is two independently-configured realms rather than two git trees, which is what house/dialect resolution can be isolated on -- its isolation assertions (one MISSING line, the healthy realm's two ok lines intact, no leak of the neighbour's name) are ones no one-realm test could make. Both residuals the second commit's message states are also stated in the tests' doc comments, so they cannot rot away from the code. Gates run and passed here: fmt, clippy, full workspace tests, bundles/self, bundles/verify, release build. scripts/coverage-exact.sh is recorded pending for host/CI per the release configuration -- its boundary tests need a namespace the box deliberately refuses to nest; not skipped, not lowered.

cargo test --workspace: 65 successful test-suite summaries, 0 failed; cargo run -p brokkr-cli -- compile --bundle bundles/self: 1 bundle compiled, 0 failed (offline from the bound Cargo registry cache)

members.correctness: Correctness review of 8c80277 and 68116ee found two medium evidence gaps; no files were changed except this required result. (1) crates/brokkr-cli/src/doctor/tests.rs:410-540 does not make the doctor proof load-bearing for distinct realm trees. If the docs realm is repointed to app, the dialect case still reports docs unusable because app/broken.json is missing, and the house case still reports docs/missing.md missing; all current assertions continue to pass because neither checks the resolved docs path or distinct repository identity. Thus this proof does not satisfy the review requirement that it fail when both realms resolve to one tree. (2) crates/brokkr-runtime/src/engine/tests.rs:4150-4238 does not prove realm_facts carries each repository's own dirty-worktree state: both repositories are clean, only alpha's false value is asserted, and beta's dirty_worktrees value is never asserted. A regression that always probes one repository, or always reports false, would pass, leaving the claimed per-realm dirty-worktree evidence incomplete. The distinct HEAD/path/hearth assertions for World, realms, runs, and muninn are otherwise substantive; the seven named tests and all recorded validation gates passed, frozen paths are untouched, and no security residual was found.
members.security: Security review of 8c80277 and 68116ee (origin/main..HEAD), read-only, no edits. Production delta is one line: crates/brokkr-runtime/src/realms.rs widens the #[cfg(test)] tests module to pub(crate) so engine tests reuse the two-repository fixture; it compiles to nothing outside test builds. The other five files are tests only; contracts/, policy/, reference/ and fixtures/ are untouched. Injection: no parser, driver, protocol or seat-result code changed; tests feed fixed JSON through existing engine APIs. Journal: fixtures write only to tempdir hearths, carry no secrets (fake identity brokkr@test, commit.gpgSign off, only shas and realm names), and the muninn test asserts both hearths are byte-identical after the overseer read (0026 ruling 5). Fail-closed: the engine test asserts a beta run handed alpha's reviewed heads yields drift_detected true at world and realm level; doctor tests assert a broken realm makes the report unhealthy. Nothing weakened. Tamper: fixtures shell out to git from PATH inside tempdirs, the same pattern as pre-existing helpers git_repo/git_commit; test-only. Fixture honesty: two git init trees with distinct file, content and message, assert_ne on the shas, and assertions (one head printed once, neighbour's sha absent, realm_facts keyed only by the run's own realm) that would fail on a one-tree world. All seven new tests pass in .forge/test-run.log. Non-security note for the correctness member: the doctor house readout is one world-wide count and a broken neighbour suppresses the healthy realm's line; the report still goes unhealthy so there is no fail-open, and the branch records this as a residual inside the test itself.

result.notes: Answered both medium residuals the correctness review returned; committed 740c462 (tests only, signed). (1) doctor: the two-realm proofs were green for the wrong reason - repointing docs at app kept every assertion true. Both now plant a decoy of the same relative name in the neighbour's tree (a usable dialect at app/broken.json via a new realm_local_dialect helper; a readable app/missing.md), assert the resolved path each failure names is under docs' own tree and not app's, and carry the one-tree world as an explicit control at the foot of the test - which is also what proves the decoy is genuinely usable. Verified by mutation: with docs repointed to app both tests fail on !report.healthy, the whole proof and not a path string. (2) engine realm_facts: beta is now left dirty and alpha clean for the length of realm_facts_key_two_repositories_by_their_own_realm_and_never_cross, so alpha's run asserts false while its neighbour is dirty and beta's asserts true, with each run's world-wide dirty_worktrees asserted beside its realm-keyed one. Verified by mutation on engine.rs: a probe hard-wired to beta breaks alpha's assertion, a probe hard-wired to false breaks beta's; the production line was restored and the branch's only non-test line remains the #[cfg(test)] pub(crate) widening. Scope held: no schema version, no contract, no engine behaviour change, no new flag; contracts/, policy/, reference/, fixtures/ untouched; the two documented residuals (world-wide house count, one realm key per run) left as findings. Gates run on the committed tree: cargo fmt --all -- --check clean; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings clean; cargo test --workspace --all-features --locked 65 test binaries, 0 failures (.forge/test-run.log); compile --bundle bundles/self and bundles/verify both ok; cargo build --release --locked -p brokkr-cli ok. scripts/coverage-exact.sh is PENDING host/CI - the boundary tests need a namespace this box refuses to nest; it was not lowered or skipped silently. Nothing pushed.

members.correctness: Reviewed all three commits from origin/main through 740c462 for correctness and fit. The change is tests/fixtures only apart from cfg(test) visibility; frozen contracts, policy, schemas, fixtures, and reference bytes are untouched. The two-repository fixtures have distinct trees and HEADs, and the realm/path, realms CLI, doctor decoys, realm_facts head/drift/dirty state, runs grouping, and Muninn citations contain assertions that fail under one-tree or wrong-tree resolution. All seven changed proof cases passed; no correctness, fit, or security findings.
members.security: Security review of origin/main..HEAD (8c80277, 68116ee and the in-run 740c462), read-only, no edits, nothing committed. Production delta is still the single line in crates/brokkr-runtime/src/realms.rs that widens the #[cfg(test)] tests module to pub(crate); it compiles to nothing outside test builds and exposes no production surface. The other five files are tests only; contracts/, policy/, reference/ and fixtures/ are untouched (diff --stat confirms only crates/). Injection: no parser, driver, protocol or seat-result code changed; every payload the tests feed the engine is fixed JSON, git is invoked via Command::new with literal args (no shell), and the feature string with an apostrophe in muninn.rs goes through argv, not a shell. Journal: all hearths live under tempfile::tempdir (Workspace::new in both CLI suites and the runtime fixture); fixtures carry no secrets (fake identity brokkr@test, commit.gpgSign off, repo-local config only, never --global); the muninn test asserts both hearths are byte-identical after the overseer read (0026 ruling 5) and the realms verb test asserts no journal file is created. Fail-closed: 740c462 strengthens rather than weakens - the engine test now leaves beta dirty and alpha clean and asserts each realm's own dirty_worktrees at realm and world level, and still asserts a beta run handed alpha's reviewed heads yields drift_detected true; the doctor tests plant a usable decoy of the same relative name in the neighbour's tree so a realm resolved to the wrong tree would go healthy, assert !report.healthy and the resolved path under the realm's own tree, and carry the one-tree world as an explicit control that goes healthy only because the decoy is genuinely usable. The new realm_local_dialect helper copies the repo's dialects/openspec.json and instructions into the tempdir (read from repo, written to tempdir only). Tamper: no path escapes the tempdir; the helpers shell out to git from PATH inside tempdirs, the same pre-existing pattern as git_repo/git_commit (inherits host global git config such as hooks path - test-only, pre-existing, info at most, not a residual of this branch). Fixture honesty from the security side: every fixture asserts assert_ne on the two shas, distinct file name/content/message guarantee distinct trees, and the head assertions (one head printed once, neighbour's sha absent, realm_facts keyed only by the run's own realm, recorded_heads differing across hearths) plus the doctor one-tree controls would fail on a one-tree world. Ran the seven new tests on this head: all pass (brokkr-runtime 2, doctor 2, tests/realms.rs 2, tests/muninn.rs 1); the verify seat's result (11:18:35 UTC) post-dates 740c462 (11:17:33 UTC). Non-security residuals the branch documents in-test (world-wide house count, one realm key per run) are observability gaps in the fail-closed direction and belong to the correctness member and a later ruling.
